hints.title: Forward Sequence Coupling
hints.text: Selecting which balloon to burst first causes remaining balloons on either side to become new neighbors, making future gains depend on actions taken in adjacent segments. Why does choosing an initial burst prevent subproblems from remaining independent?

hints.title: Inverting Time to Last Burst
hints.text: Frame the decision in reverse by selecting which balloon in a bounded interval will be burst last. Because that balloon remains present until every other balloon in the interval is gone, it acts as a fixed boundary that isolates the left and right subproblems.

hints.title: Interval Recurrence Relation
hints.text: Pad the array with 1 at both boundaries and let dp[i][j] represent the maximum coins from bursting all balloons strictly between index i and j. For intervals of increasing length, compute dp[left][right] by testing each balloon k between left and right as the last burst, taking the maximum of dp[left][k] + dp[k][right] + nums[left] * nums[k] * nums[right].
